text: Editorial and Medical Review PolicyAt Irving Health and Wellness Clinic, clients across Irving and the surrounding area count on our website for clear, trustworthy health and wellness information. Because that information can shape real decisions about your care, we hold every page to a clear standard for how it is written, reviewed, and kept current. This page explains how we work.Who writes our contentOur articles and service pages are written and maintained by the Irving Health and Wellness Clinic editorial team. Our writers research each topic using trusted medical sources, then write it in plain language so it is easy to understand.How our content is medically reviewedBefore we publish anything that covers a medical or treatment topic, a qualified medical professional on our team reviews it for accuracy and clarity.Reviewed by: Lori Secerovic, APRN, FNP-COur reviewer checks that the content reflects current medical guidance, that treatments and their benefits and risks are described correctly, and that nothing could mislead you about your options.The sources we rely onWe base our health content on respected, authoritative sources, including:Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)National Institutes of Health (NIH) and MedlinePlusU.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)Professional medical and specialty associationsPeer-reviewed medical journals and established clinical guidelinesWhen we state a fact or a statistic, we aim to link it back to the original source so you can read more.How often we update our contentMedical guidance changes over time. We review our health content regularly and refresh it at least once a year, or sooner when new research or guidance appears. Where possible, a page shows when it was last reviewed or updated.Corrections and feedbackIf something looks inaccurate or out of date, we want to hear about it. Reach out through our contact page and our team will look into it promptly.A note about your careThe information on this site is for general education only. It is not a diagnosis or a treatment plan for your specific situation. Before starting any treatment or changing your care, please talk with a qualified provider. To discuss your goals, you can book a consultation with our team.

text: Skinvive vs Dermal Filler: Which One Do You Actually Need? By Irving H&W Clinic July 28, 2026 Medical Aesthetics Table of Contents Key Takeaways:Skinvive improves skin quality and hydration. It does not add volume.Dermal fillers restore lost volume and reshape features.Many people assume they need filler when their actual concern is skin texture. Skinvive gets called “a filler” constantly, including by people selling it. It is not one, and the confusion leads people to book the wrong treatment.Both are hyaluronic acid injectables. What they do with that hyaluronic acid is completely different, and that difference decides which one you need.What is Skinvive and how is it different from filler?Skinvive by Juvederm is a hyaluronic acid microdroplet injectable. The FDA approved it in May 2023 to improve skin smoothness of the cheeks in adults over 21, and it was the first product of its kind approved in the US.Rather than filling a specific line or hollow, it is placed as many tiny droplets across the treatment area. The goal is hydration, elasticity, and surface smoothness rather than shape.Does Skinvive add volume to the face?No. This is the single most important thing to understand about it.The droplets are too small and placed too superficially to lift or plump anything. If your concern is a deep fold, a flat cheek, or a thin lip, Skinvive is the wrong tool no matter how well it is marketed.Skinvive vs dermal filler: side by sideThe two products solve different problems, which the table makes clear.SkinviveDermal fillerWhat it doesHydrates, smooths skin surfaceRestores volume, reshapes featuresPlacementMany microdroplets, superficialTargeted deeper placementVisible changeGlow and texture, subtleStructural, visible in shapeBest forDull, crepey, dehydrated skinFolds, hollows, lips, contourDurationUp to 6 monthsVaries by product and areaPrice here$700 per syringe$800 for 1 syringe, $1,520 for 2The practical question at consultation is simple. Is the issue the surface of your skin, or the shape underneath it?What skin concerns does Skinvive treat?It suits skin that looks tired rather than sunken. Dullness, fine crepey texture, and dehydration that skincare alone has not fixed.In the clinical study behind the approval, patients reported higher satisfaction with how glowing, hydrated, refreshed, and healthy their skin looked. Those words describe surface quality, not shape, which is exactly the product’s lane.“One key way to improve skin quality is by enhancing hydration. SKINVIVE by JUVEDERM is truly innovative because it works beneath the skin’s surface to increase skin hydration improving skin quality,” said Macrene Alexiades, MD, PhD, dual US-EU board-certified dermatologist and lead investigator of the Skinvive clinical trial, in AbbVie’s approval announcement.How is Skinvive injected?It is placed as a series of very small injections spaced roughly half a centimeter to a centimeter apart across the cheeks.The appointment is quick, and downtime is minimal. Expect small raised bumps at the injection points that settle within a day or two, and the usual chance of minor bruising.How long does Skinvive last?Up to six months with optimal treatment. Repeat sessions maintain the effect.That is shorter than most volumizing fillers, which is consistent with how superficially it sits and how it is metabolized.Can you get Skinvive and filler in the same visit?Yes, and the combination makes sense more often than either alone. They are complementary because they work at different depths on different problems.A common plan treats lost volume with filler first, then uses Skinvive for surface quality. Our dermal fillers page covers the volume side in detail.Is Skinvive approved for the neck?In June 2026 the FDA approved Skinvive for the appearance of neck lines, making it the first hyaluronic acid injectable with that indication. It is a genuinely new development in an area that previously had few good injectable options.Our clinic currently offers Skinvive for its cheek indication. If neck treatment is something you are interested in, ask at consultation and we will tell you honestly whether and when we offer it.What are the side effects of Skinvive?The common reactions are local and short-lived.Small bumps at the injection points for a day or twoRedness, tenderness, or minor bruisingTemporary unevenness while the droplets settleCan it be reversed?Yes. Like other hyaluronic acid products, it can be dissolved with hyaluronidase if ever needed, which is part of why HA injectables are considered a lower-risk category.Who is a good candidate for Skinvive?Someone whose skin looks dull or crepey but whose facial volume is fine. Often that is a person in their late twenties to forties who is not ready for filler and does not need it.It also suits filler patients who have volume handled and want the skin itself to match. It is not a substitute for treating deep folds or significant volume loss.How much does Skinvive cost?Skinvive is $700 per syringe at our Irving clinic. Dermal fillers are $800 for one syringe and $1,520 for two.If you are unsure which you need, book a consultation before committing to either. The consultation is free, and choosing the wrong product is not.Frequently Asked QuestionsIs Skinvive the same as a skin booster?Skin booster is the generic category name used internationally. Skinvive is the specific product that holds the FDA approval in the US, which matters because approval means the claims were tested against a placebo.How soon will you see results?Expect the visible improvement to build over a few weeks as hydration improves, rather than an instant change on the day. Judge it at the one-month mark.Does Skinvive help with acne scars or pores?It can soften the look of fine texture, but it does not treat scarring. Depressed acne scars respond better to microneedling, which works by rebuilding collagen rather than adding hydration.Skinvive or Botox for smoother skin?They do different jobs. Botox relaxes the muscles that crease the skin, while Skinvive hydrates the skin itself. Lines caused by expression need Botox; texture and dullness point to Skinvive.Which one do you actually need?If the shape of your face has changed, that is a filler conversation. If the shape is fine but the skin surface looks tired, that is Skinvive.Plenty of people need neither yet, and we will say so. Book through our aesthetic treatments page or call 972-891-8650 and we will look at your skin before recommending anything. text: How Many Laser Hair Removal Sessions Do You Need? Area by Area By Irving H&W Clinic July 27, 2026 Medical Aesthetics Table of Contents Key Takeaways:Most people need six to nine sessions for best results, not one or two.Sessions are spaced roughly six weeks apart because only growing hairs respond.Laser gives permanent hair reduction, not permanent removal. The single most common surprise with laser hair removal is the number of visits. People book expecting one session and a smooth result.That is not how the hair growth cycle works, and understanding why makes the schedule and the pricing make sense.How many laser hair removal sessions do most people need?Most people need six to nine treatments for the best result, according to the American Society for Laser Medicine and Surgery. Some see good clearance at four to six.Cleveland Clinic puts the typical course at four to six sessions spaced six weeks apart, which can take up to nine months from start to finish.Why does laser hair removal take more than one session?The laser only works on hair that is actively growing. Hair in its resting or shedding phase has no pigment connection to the follicle for the laser to target.At any given moment only a portion of the hair in an area is in that growth phase. Each session catches whatever is growing that day, which is why the course is spread out.How far apart should sessions be scheduled?Around six weeks for most body areas. Facial hair cycles faster and is often treated every four weeks.Going sooner wastes a session, because the next batch of follicles has not entered the growth phase yet. Going much later is less of a problem, though it can stretch the total timeline.How many sessions for legs, underarms, bikini, and face?Coarse, dense hair on the body tends to respond faster than fine or hormonally driven hair on the face.AreaTypical sessionsSpacingUnderarms6 to 8Every 6 weeksBikini or Brazilian6 to 8Every 6 weeksLower legs6 to 8Every 6 to 8 weeksBack or chest8 or moreEvery 6 to 8 weeksFace, upper lip or chin8 or moreEvery 4 weeksThe American Academy of Dermatology lists the chest, back, shoulders, neck, bikini line and face as suitable areas, with the exception of skin around the eyes.Does hair color change how many sessions you need?Yes, more than almost any other factor. The laser targets pigment in the follicle, so dark coarse hair responds best.Grey, white, red and very blonde hair have little pigment to absorb the light. Laser is generally not effective on those, regardless of how many sessions you book.Does skin tone affect laser hair removal?It affects which device is appropriate rather than whether you are a candidate. Modern systems safely treat a wide range of skin tones when settings and wavelength are matched correctly.This is one of the clearest arguments for having it done in a medical setting rather than wherever is cheapest.“Because of its popularity, laser hair removal might seem like a procedure that anyone can do, but in the wrong hands, it can cause serious skin damage,” says Carolyn I. Jacob, MD, FAAD, board-certified dermatologist and Associate Clinical Instructor of Dermatology at Northwestern’s Feinberg School of Medicine, in an American Academy of Dermatology news release.How much hair is gone after the first session?Expect a 10% to 25% reduction after the first treatment, per the American Academy of Dermatology. Results build with each subsequent session.Shedding in the one to three weeks after a session is normal and is often mistaken for regrowth.Is laser hair removal permanent?It gives permanent hair reduction, not permanent removal. That distinction matters and is often blurred in advertising.Treated follicles that are destroyed do not regrow. Some follicles survive, and hormonal changes can activate new ones later, so most people need occasional maintenance.Do you need maintenance sessions?Usually one or two a year after finishing the initial course. Some people need none for years.Hormonal shifts from pregnancy, menopause, or conditions such as PCOS can trigger new growth. Our guide to PCOS root causes covers why that happens.What should you do before and after a session?Preparation changes your result more than most people expect.Shave the area the day before, since the laser needs the follicle intact below the skinDo not wax, pluck or thread for four weeks beforehand, as that removes the targetAvoid sun exposure and self-tanner before and after treatmentWhat about aftercare?Expect redness and slight bumps for a day or two. Skip hot tubs, saunas and heavy workouts for 24 hours, and use sunscreen on any exposed treated area.“If you experience any pain or discoloration after receiving laser hair removal, see a board-certified dermatologist right away,” Jacob advises in the same release.When does a package cost less than single sessions?Our laser hair removal pricing runs by area size, from $200 for an extra-small area up to $450 for a large area per session. There is also a full hair removal bundle at $8,500.Since the typical course is six to nine sessions, the arithmetic favors a package once you are treating several areas rather than one. We work the numbers with you at consultation rather than guessing.Frequently Asked QuestionsDoes laser hair removal hurt?Most people describe it as a rubber band snap against the skin. Underarms and bikini are the most sensitive areas, and lower legs the least. Cooling built into the device makes it manageable without numbing for most patients.Can you shave between sessions?Yes, shaving is fine and expected. Waxing, plucking and threading are not, because they remove the follicle the laser needs to target. That is the most common reason a session underperforms.Is laser hair removal safe during pregnancy?It is normally deferred until after pregnancy. There is no strong evidence of harm, but there is also little safety research, and pregnancy hormones drive hair changes that make results unpredictable.Why is my hair growing back between sessions?Some regrowth between sessions is expected and does not mean it is failing. You are treating different follicles each visit, so full clearance only appears toward the end of the course.Booking your first sessionThe useful first step is an assessment of your hair color, skin tone and the areas you want treated. That determines your realistic session count before you commit to a package.Book through our aesthetic treatments page or call 972-891-8650. text: Double Chin Treatment Without Surgery: How Kybella Works and Who It Suits By Irving H&W Clinic July 27, 2026 Medical Aesthetics Table of Contents Key Takeaways:Kybella is an injectable that destroys fat cells under the chin, and it is the only FDA-approved drug for that use.Most people need more than one session, spaced at least a month apart.Swelling after treatment is expected and is part of how it works. A double chin is stubborn in a way that frustrates people. It often stays put through weight loss, and it shows up in photos from angles nobody chooses.This guide covers what actually causes submental fat, how the non-surgical options compare, and who Kybella suits.What causes a double chin?Submental fat sits in a pocket beneath the jawline. Genetics decide how much you store there and how visible it is.Weight gain adds to it, but weight is not the whole story. Plenty of lean people have one, and plenty of people lose weight everywhere except under the chin. Age contributes too, since skin loses elasticity and the area softens.What are the non-surgical options for submental fat?There are three broad routes. An injectable that destroys the fat cells, a device that freezes them, and surgery that removes them.Only one of those is a drug approved specifically for this area. Our clinic offers the injectable route, which is Kybella.How does Kybella break down fat under the chin?Kybella is deoxycholic acid. Your body already makes it, and its normal job is helping you absorb dietary fat.Injected into a fat pocket, it works as a cytolytic drug. It physically breaks down the fat cell membrane, and the destroyed cells are cleared by the body over the following weeks.Is Kybella FDA approved?Yes. The FDA approved it in April 2015 for moderate to severe fat below the chin in adults.Approval was based on two placebo-controlled Phase III trials involving more than 1,000 adults. It remains the only injectable approved for this specific use.How many Kybella treatments will you need?More than one, in almost every case. The FDA label allows up to six treatments, spaced at least one month apart.In the clinical trials, 59% of patients received all six. Your provider maps the area and decides the number based on how much fat is there and how you respond to the first round.What happens during a Kybella appointment?The area is marked with a grid so the injections are evenly spaced. Numbing is applied first, and ice helps with comfort.The label permits up to 50 small injections in a single session. The injecting itself takes around 15 to 20 minutes.What does Kybella recovery look like?Swelling is not a side effect here so much as evidence the drug is doing its job. It is the most noticeable part of recovery.StageWhat to expectFirst 24 hoursSwelling begins, area feels tender and warmDays 2 to 4Swelling usually peaks, chin may look fuller than beforeWeek 1 to 2Swelling settles, firm lumps under the skin are commonWeeks 3 to 4Most visible swelling resolves, firmness fadesAfter 1 monthEarliest point a further session is permittedTimelines vary between people. Plan your first session well ahead of any event you care about.How does Kybella compare to fat freezing and a neck lift?Each targets the same fat with a different mechanism, cost, and downtime.KybellaFat freezingNeck liftTypeInjectable drugCooling deviceSurgeryAnesthesiaTopical numbingNoneGeneral or localSessionsUp to 6Usually 1 to 3One procedureDowntimeSwelling for days to weeksMinimalWeeksTreats loose skinNoNoYesOffered hereYesNoNoIf loose skin rather than fat is the main issue, none of the fat treatments will fix it. That is worth establishing at consultation before you spend anything.Are Kybella results permanent?The treated fat cells are destroyed and do not come back. In that sense the result is lasting.You can still gain weight, and the remaining cells in the area can enlarge. Most people who keep their weight stable do not need repeat rounds.What are the side effects of Kybella?Most reactions are local and temporary. The trial data gives useful numbers rather than vague reassurance.Bruising affected 72% of trial subjectsSwelling, pain, numbness, and firmness at the site are commonNerve injury causing an uneven smile occurred in 4%, and every case resolved on its ownHow long did the rarer effects last?In the trials, nerve-related weakness resolved with a median of 44 days. Difficulty swallowing occurred in 2% of subjects and resolved with a median of 3 days.Who is not a good candidate for Kybella?It is not for everyone. The label specifically warns against use where infection is present at the injection site.Anyone with a current or previous history of difficulty swallowing should avoid it, since treatment can worsen that. It is also not appropriate if your concern is loose skin rather than fat.How much does Kybella cost?Kybella is $600 per treatment at our Irving clinic. Because most people need several sessions, budget for the full course rather than one visit.Insurance does not cover it, since it is a cosmetic treatment. We give you an expected session count at consultation so the total is clear upfront.Frequently Asked QuestionsDoes Kybella tighten loose skin?No. It treats fat only. If skin laxity is the main issue, a fat treatment will not improve it and may make it more noticeable. This is the single most common reason we tell someone Kybella is not right for them.How soon will you see results?Most people see a visible change after two to four treatments. Because swelling masks the result early on, judge progress about a month after each session rather than in the first week.Does Kybella hurt?There is stinging and burning during the injections and for a short time afterward. Numbing cream and ice make it manageable. Most people describe it as uncomfortable rather than severe.Can Kybella be used elsewhere on the body?Fat below the chin is the only FDA-approved use. Anything else is off-label, and we do not offer it that way.Can you combine Kybella with other treatments?Yes, though usually not on the same day. Many people pair it with Botox or dermal fillers for the wider jawline and lower face.Is Kybella right for you?It suits people close to their goal weight with a defined pocket of fat under the chin and reasonable skin quality. It does not suit people whose main concern is sagging.The honest test is a consultation where someone examines the area and tells you which of the two you have. Book through our aesthetic treatments page or call 972-891-8650. text: NAD+ IV Therapy Benefits: What the Research Shows and What It Does Not By Irving H&W Clinic July 27, 2026 IV Therapy Table of Contents Key Takeaways:NAD+ is a coenzyme your cells use for energy production and DNA repair, and levels fall with age.IV delivery puts NAD+ straight into your bloodstream, bypassing digestion entirely.Controlled human data on IV NAD+ specifically is still limited to small pilot studies. NAD+ is the most expensive drip on most clinic menus, and the most oversold. Plenty of pages promise reversed aging and restored energy, while far fewer explain what the research has actually tested.What is NAD+ and what does it do in the body?NAD+ stands for nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide. It is a coenzyme found in every living cell, and your body cannot make energy without it. It shuttles electrons during metabolism and supports the enzymes that repair damaged DNA.NAD+ levels decline as people age. That observation is what drove the interest in replacing it.What are the benefits of NAD+ IV therapy?Clinics most often offer NAD+ for low energy, brain fog, burnout, and recovery after illness. Patients frequently report feeling clearer and more energetic in the days after a session.Those reports matter, but they are not the same as trial evidence. The honest position is that the mechanism is well understood while the clinical outcomes are still being studied.Does NAD+ IV therapy actually work?It reliably does one thing: it raises circulating NAD+ levels. That much is measurable and not in dispute.Whether raising those levels produces durable improvements in energy, cognition, or aging is not yet settled. Most published human research studies oral precursors rather than IV infusions, so the evidence does not transfer cleanly.What does the research actually show?Separating the established from the promising is the most useful thing this page can do.ClaimEvidence statusSourceNAD+ is essential to cellular energy and DNA repairEstablished biochemistryClinical Evidence for Targeting NAD Therapeutically, NIH PMCNAD+ levels decline with ageWell documentedNIH PMC reviewIV infusion raises circulating NAD+Demonstrated, small pilot trialsRandomized placebo-controlled IV NAD+ pilot, medRxivNAD+ shows promise in neurodegeneration and inflammationPromising, not proven in humansNature Aging review, 2025NAD+ IV reverses aging or treats diseaseNot supportedNo adequate human trialsA 2025 review in Nature Aging, co-authored by more than 25 researchers, named NAD+ biology one of the more promising directions in aging research. The same review was clear that clinical proof in humans is still pending.Why is NAD+ given by IV instead of a pill?Anything you swallow has to survive stomach acid and liver processing before it reaches your bloodstream. A meaningful share is lost along the way.An infusion skips that path completely, which is why clinics use it when the goal is to raise levels quickly. The same logic applies across our IV therapy menu.NAD+ IV drip vs NAD+ injection: which one fits your goal?Both deliver NAD+ past the digestive system. They differ in dose, time, and cost.NAD+ IV dripNAD+ injectionDose250mg or 500mg25mg to 200mgPrice$325 or $475$50Time in clinicLonger, dose dependentMinutesBest forA full loading dose, first-time protocolsTopping up between infusions, tighter budgetsMost people starting out do a small number of infusions first, then use injections to maintain.How long does a NAD+ infusion take?Longer than a standard vitamin drip. NAD+ has to run slowly, and the higher the dose the longer the session.Rushing it is what causes discomfort, so the drip rate is set to your tolerance rather than the clock. Your provider will give you an expected time for your specific dose when you book.What does a NAD+ drip feel like?Most people notice a flushing sensation, some warmth in the chest, or mild nausea if the drip runs too fast. It is uncomfortable rather than dangerous.The fix is simple. Slowing the infusion resolves it within a minute or two, which is why NAD+ is never rushed.What are the side effects of NAD+ IV therapy?Common effects are infusion related and stop when the session ends.Flushing, warmth, or chest tightness during the dripNausea or cramping if the rate is too fastBruising or soreness at the IV siteIs long-term use well studied?Long-term safety data for repeated high-dose NAD+ infusions is limited. A 2026 pilot study in Frontiers in Aging tracking real-world infusions reported abdominal cramping, nausea, increased heart rate, and chest pressure during NAD+ drips, and found infusions of the precursor NR were better tolerated. That is another reason to treat it as supportive care rather than a standing prescription.Who should not get NAD+ IV therapy?NAD+ infusions are not appropriate for everyone. Skip it or seek specific clearance if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, have kidney or heart failure, or are being treated for an active cancer.Anyone on multiple prescription medications should have a provider review the plan first. Our intake includes a medical screen for exactly this reason.How often should you get NAD+ IV therapy?There is no evidence-backed universal schedule. Clinics commonly run a short series of infusions close together, then move to spaced maintenance.The sensible approach is to treat the first series as a trial and judge by how you actually feel. Our guide on how often to get IV vitamin therapy covers the same reasoning across drip types.How much does NAD+ IV therapy cost?NAD+ 250mg is $325 and NAD+ 500mg is $475. A NAD+ injection ranging from 25mg to 200mg is $50.Insurance does not cover wellness infusions. Given the cost, it is worth ruling out cheaper explanations for low energy first, including sleep, thyroid function, and B12 status.Frequently Asked QuestionsIs NAD+ IV therapy FDA approved?No. NAD+ is not approved as a drug to treat aging, fatigue, or any specific condition. It is used in wellness settings, which is a different regulatory category and a reason to be cautious about strong claims.Can you take an NAD+ supplement instead?Oral precursors such as NR and NMN are widely sold and carry most of the published human research. They raise NAD+ more slowly than an infusion. For many people they are a reasonable and far cheaper starting point.How soon would you feel a difference?Some people report a lift within a day or two. Others notice nothing after a full series. Because the response varies this much, we suggest judging it after a defined trial rather than committing to a long protocol upfront.Is NAD+ safe to use long term?Unknown. Short-term infusions appear well tolerated in the studies published so far, but there is no good long-term safety data on repeated high doses.Will NAD+ help my fatigue?It might, if your fatigue has a metabolic component. It will not correct fatigue caused by poor sleep, thyroid disease, anemia, or a hormone imbalance. Our guide to IV therapy for chronic fatigue walks through those causes.Is NAD+ worth trying?It depends on what you expect from it. As a supportive option for energy and recovery, alongside sleep, labs, and nutrition, it is reasonable to try with clear expectations.As a treatment for aging or a substitute for a diagnosis, the evidence does not support it. If you want to talk it through, book a consultation or call 972-891-8650. text: Not Losing Weight on Semaglutide? 5 Research-Backed Reasons and Fixes By Irving H&W Clinic July 21, 2026 Medical Weight Loss Table of Contents Key takeaway: A stalled scale on semaglutide is common and usually fixable. The most frequent causes are a dose that never reached its effective level, a natural plateau that arrives after months of steady loss, habits the medication cannot override, or biology that responds better to a different medication. Each one has a specific, evidence-backed fix.Semaglutide has better trial results than almost anything that came before it. It is also not magic. In the landmark STEP 1 trial of 1,961 adults, participants on weekly 2.4 mg semaglutide lost 14.9% of their body weight on average over 68 weeks. But inside that average sits a quieter number: 86.4% of participants lost at least 5% of their weight, which means roughly 1 in 7 did not. If your progress has stalled, you are not imagining it, and you are not alone. Here is what the research says is actually going on.Is Your Semaglutide Dose High Enough?The trial results people quote came from the full 2.4 mg weekly dose, reached after 16 weeks of step-up increases. Many stalled patients turn out to be sitting at an early titration dose, sometimes for months. The medication is working exactly as expected; it simply was never raised to the level that produced the famous numbers.This is the first thing to review with your provider. If side effects blocked earlier increases, a slower ramp or a different escalation schedule often gets you the rest of the way. Our semaglutide program reviews dose against progress every month for exactly this reason.When Does Weight Loss Plateau on Semaglutide?In STEP 1, average weight loss flattened in the final months of the 68-week trial. That plateau is not failure. It is the body reaching a new equilibrium: as you lose weight, you burn fewer calories at rest, appetite signals adapt, and the same dose now maintains rather than reduces.The distinction that matters is timing. A plateau after 8 to 12 months of steady loss is physiology. A stall in the first 3 months, at a full dose, is a signal to look deeper at the causes below.3 Habits That Stall Weight Loss on SemaglutideSemaglutide quiets appetite. It does not choose what you eat, lift weights for you, or put you to bed on time. Three habits show up over and over in stalled patients:Too little protein. Eating much less overall means protein needs jump proportionally. Low protein accelerates muscle loss, which drags your resting metabolism down with it.No resistance training. A meaningful share of rapid weight loss can come from lean mass. Muscle is the tissue that keeps your calorie burn up after the loss, and strength training is how you keep it.Short sleep and unmanaged stress. Both push hunger hormones in the wrong direction and quietly raise intake. The habits that protect weight loss long-term are the same ones that break plateaus.Medical Reasons Semaglutide Stops WorkingWeight is regulated by overlapping hormone systems, and a stall is sometimes the first visible sign of one of them. Untreated insulin resistance, thyroid dysfunction, and sex-hormone imbalances can all blunt progress on a GLP-1 medication. This is why a labs-first program matters: bloodwork drawn before and during treatment tells you whether the plateau is behavioral, pharmacologic, or hormonal.Semaglutide Non-Responders: When Switching Makes SenseTrue non-response is real, and the researchers who ran the biggest trials say so plainly.“Even though drugs like tirzepatide and semaglutide work really well, better than anything we have ever seen, we still have people who don’t respond to them. So, moving forward, we want to keep trying to do better.”Dr. Louis Aronne, Comprehensive Weight Control Center | Weill Cornell MedicineNon-response to semaglutide does not predict non-response to everything. In the 72-week head-to-head trial, tirzepatide produced 20.2% average weight loss versus 13.7% for semaglutide, and twice as many participants reached a 25% reduction. Patients who plateau on semaglutide sometimes see renewed progress after a supervised switch to tirzepatide, which works on two hormone receptors instead of one. The full comparison is in our semaglutide vs tirzepatide breakdown.How to Restart Weight Loss on SemaglutideConfirm your current dose and how long you have been on it. Below full dose, the next step is usually titration, not switching.Track body composition, not just the scale. Losing fat while holding muscle can read as a “stall” on a bathroom scale.Audit protein, strength training, and sleep for two honest weeks before concluding the medication stopped working.Get labs if you have not had them since starting. Thyroid, fasting insulin, and HbA1c can each explain a plateau.If you are at full dose with clean labs and honest habits, ask your provider about a supervised switch. That conversation is a normal part of good care, not a failure.FAQsHow long should I wait before deciding semaglutide is not working?Give the medication a fair trial at a therapeutic dose. Most providers look for at least 5% weight loss after roughly 3 months at full dose. Stalling during early titration weeks is normal and not a verdict on the medication.Is it normal to stop losing weight after a year?Yes. Trial data shows average loss flattening near the end of the first year as the body reaches a new set point. At that stage the goal shifts from losing to maintaining, which is a success, not a stall.Will increasing the dose restart my weight loss?Sometimes, if you are below the full therapeutic dose. That decision belongs with your provider, because it depends on your current dose, side effects, and labs. Never adjust a GLP-1 dose on your own.Should I switch to tirzepatide if semaglutide stalled?It is one evidence-backed option among several. The head-to-head trial favored tirzepatide on every weight measure, but dose, habits, and underlying conditions should be ruled out first. A supervised transition keeps side effects predictable if you do switch.Get Your Plateau Properly EvaluatedA plateau is information, not defeat. Our medical weight loss program in Irving treats it that way: labs, body composition, dose history, and habits reviewed together, then a specific next step instead of a shrug. Book a consultation and bring your story with you. text: Hormone Pellets vs Injections vs Creams: Pros, Cons, and How to Choose By Irving H&W Clinic July 21, 2026 Hormone Replacement Therapy Table of Contents Quick answer: Pellets give the steadiest hormone levels and need attention only every 3 to 4 months, but the dose cannot be changed once implanted. Injections are inexpensive and easy to adjust, but levels rise and fall between doses. Creams are gentle and flexible, but daily and easy to forget. The right fit depends on your labs, your schedule, and how your body responds.If you have decided to explore hormone therapy, the next question surprises most people. It is not “which hormone?” Your labs answer that. It is “how should it get into your body?” Pellets, injections, and creams can all deliver the same bioidentical hormones. What changes is the rhythm: how steady your levels stay, how often you think about dosing, and how quickly your provider can correct course.How Hormone Pellets, Injections, and Creams WorkAll three methods exist to solve the same problem: your body expects hormones on a steady drip, not in bursts. Each method approximates that drip differently.Pellets are rice-sized cylinders placed under the skin of the hip in a short in-office procedure. They dissolve slowly and release hormones continuously for roughly 3 to 6 months.Injections deliver a depot of hormone into muscle or fat, typically every week or two for testosterone. Levels peak in the first days, then decline until the next dose.Creams and gels absorb through the skin daily. Levels follow your application habits, which makes consistency the whole game.Pellets vs Injections vs Creams: Comparison ChartPelletsInjectionsCreams / GelsDosing rhythmEvery 3 to 6 monthsWeekly to biweeklyDailyLevel stabilitySteadiest, no weekly swingsPeak after the shot, trough before the nextSteady if applied consistentlyDose adjustabilityLowest: cannot change until the pellet dissolvesHigh: adjust at any doseHighest: adjust day to dayProcedure involvedMinor in-office insertion, small incisionQuick needle stickNoneCommon frictionInsertion-site soreness, rare pellet extrusionMood or energy dips before the next doseSkipped days, transfer to partners or childrenWho tends to prefer itPeople who want to stop thinking about dosingPeople who want control and lower costNeedle-averse patients starting low and slowHormone Pellet Therapy: Pros and ConsThe strongest argument for pellets is the absence of a cycle. There is no shot day, no pre-dose slump, no daily application to remember. For patients whose symptoms return every time they miss a dose, that steadiness is the entire point.The trade-off is commitment. Once a pellet is implanted, the dose is fixed until it dissolves. If your level runs high or side effects appear, there is no simple way to dial it back. That is why careful, conservative dosing from your baseline labs matters more with pellets than with any other method. It is also why the insertion should follow bloodwork, not a sales script.Hormone Injections: Pros and ConsInjections remain the workhorse of testosterone therapy for a reason. They are inexpensive, widely available in FDA-approved forms, and easy to fine-tune. If your 6-week labs show you are running high, next week’s dose simply comes down.The trade-off is the wave pattern. Levels climb after each shot and fall before the next one, and some patients feel that fall as fatigue, irritability, or low motivation. Splitting into smaller, more frequent doses flattens the wave for many people, which is exactly the kind of adjustment a monitored program can make.Hormone Creams and Gels: Pros and ConsDaily creams and gels produce the most physiologic rhythm of all when used perfectly, and they are the easiest to stop or adjust. They suit patients starting cautiously, and women managing perimenopause symptoms who want room to titrate slowly.The trade-offs are human ones. Absorption varies from person to person and day to day. Missed applications show up as symptom swings. And residue can transfer to partners, children, or pets through skin contact in the hours after application.Compounded vs FDA-Approved Hormones: What Medical Societies SayDelivery method is only half the question. The other half is whether the preparation itself is FDA-approved or custom-compounded, and the major societies have taken a clear position on that. The Endocrine Society and ACOG both recommend FDA-approved formulations whenever one exists, because compounded preparations are not tested for consistency the same way.“Pellets can cause high hormonal peaks and prolonged elevations, which are not well monitored.”Wender et al., peer-reviewed pellet safety review, 2025 | PubMed CentralNote what that criticism targets: unmonitored dosing, more than the method itself. It is exactly why baseline labs, conservative starting doses, and scheduled rechecks matter more with pellets than with any other option. Dr. Stephanie Faubion, director of the Mayo Clinic Center for Women’s Health, has cautioned that there is “no real benefit” and “potential harm” in unregulated hormone preparations. The practical takeaway is not that any single method is wrong. It is that formulation, dosing, and monitoring deserve the same scrutiny as the delivery route. Ask any provider which formulation they use, how the starting dose is set, and when your levels get rechecked. Good clinics answer all three without hesitation.How to Choose Between Pellets, Injections, and CreamsHow do you handle routines? If daily steps fail you, creams will too. If you dread appointments, pellet reinsertions may lapse. Match the method to your real habits, not your ideal ones.How much adjustment will you likely need? First-time patients often benefit from starting on an adjustable method, then switching to pellets once their effective dose is proven and stable.How do you respond to swings? If you feel every trough between injections, steadier delivery is worth prioritizing. Your symptom pattern between doses is data. Bring it to your provider.FAQsDo pellets work better than injections?Neither is universally better. Pellets deliver steadier levels with less effort, while injections offer more control and lower cost. Head-to-head, the deciding factors are your response, your schedule, and how much dose adjustment you need in the first months of therapy.How long do hormone pellets last?Most patients get roughly 3 to 4 months from testosterone pellets, and some closer to 6. Metabolism, activity level, and dose all affect the timeline. Symptoms returning early is a signal to recheck labs, not simply to implant a larger dose.Can I switch delivery methods later?Yes, and switching is common. Many patients start on injections or creams while their effective dose is being established, then move to pellets for convenience. The reverse also happens when someone wants finer control. Timing the switch around your labs keeps levels steady.Are hormone pellets FDA-approved?Some are, and some are not. An FDA-approved testosterone pellet exists for men, while many pellets, especially estradiol pellets for women, are custom-compounded. That is exactly why the Endocrine Society and ACOG advise asking which formulation you are getting before starting therapy.Get a Recommendation Built on Your LabsThe honest answer to “which method is best” is always personal: it depends on your bloodwork, your symptoms, and your life. Our hormone therapy program in Irving starts with a full panel, walks through every delivery option, and monitors your levels after you choose, so the method serves the dose and not the other way around. text: Heat Illness at FIFA World Cup 2026 Matches in Arlington, TX: A Spectator’s Safety Guide By Irving H&W Clinic May 22, 2026 IV Therapy Table of Contents The FIFA World Cup 2026 runs from June 11 to July 19 across the United States, Canada, and Mexico. AT&T Stadium in Arlington is one of 11 US host venues, putting hundreds of thousands of soccer spectators (many flying in from cooler climates) into peak Texas summer heat.Even with the stadium roof closed during a match, the hours of pre-match tailgating, walking through massive parking lots, and outdoor FanFest events add up. The CDC classifies this kind of exposure as a serious risk for dehydration and heat-related illness, especially for visitors who have not had time to acclimatize.This guide explains how to spot warning signs, the critical difference between heat exhaustion and heat stroke, what to bring, and when to call 911 versus seeking lower-acuity care near Irving, Las Colinas, and the broader DFW area.TL;DRHeat illness at World Cup matches progresses fast, especially for fans who are not used to Texas summer. Early warning signs are thirst, dark urine, headache, and dizziness. Move to shade or air conditioning, sip cool water with electrolytes, and cool the skin. If a person develops confusion, stops sweating, or has a body temperature above 103°F, call 911. That is heat stroke, and minutes matter.Why Is Heat Illness a Real Risk at Arlington’s World Cup Matches?AT&T Stadium hosts World Cup matches during the hottest weeks of the Texas year. Late-June and July afternoons in Arlington routinely exceed 95°F, with heat indices above 105°F when humidity rises. Even when the retractable roof is closed during the match, hours of pre-game tailgating, walking through parking lots, and any outdoor FanFest activities expose spectators to severe heat. The National Weather Service classifies these conditions inside the “extreme caution” or “danger” range for heat illness.Three local factors raise the risk further:Visitors are not heat-acclimatized. Fans flying in from Europe, South America, or the northern US arrive with no preparation for 100°F days. The CDC notes that heat acclimatization takes 7 to 14 days of gradual exposure. A traveler who lands the day before a match has none of it, which puts them at materially higher risk than locals.Pavement and sun reflection. Stadium parking lots and walkways in direct sun can run 30°F to 60°F hotter than the air temperature.Sustained outdoor time. Counting tailgating, walk-in, the match itself, and walk-out, total time on the property on match day is commonly five to seven hours.What Are the Earliest Signs of Dehydration?The National Institutes of Health (MedlinePlus) lists the earliest signs of dehydration as thirst, dry mouth, fatigue, lightheadedness on standing, and urine that looks darker than pale yellow. Headache and muscle cramps often follow. By the time you feel very thirsty, you are already mildly dehydrated.Watch for any of these at a match:Persistent thirstDry mouth or lipsDark yellow or amber urineHeadacheDizziness or lightheadedness on standingFatigue out of proportion to activityMuscle cramps in legs or abdomenHow Do I Tell Heat Exhaustion from Heat Stroke?Heat exhaustion looks like heavy sweating, weakness, headache, nausea, and a fast pulse. The person is alert and oriented. Heat stroke is different. Skin may be hot and either wet or dry, body temperature climbs above 103°F, and the person becomes confused, slurred, or unresponsive. Heat stroke is a 911 emergency.Heat exhaustion: urgent but not immediately life-threateningSigns include heavy sweating, cool or pale clammy skin, a fast weak pulse, nausea or vomiting, muscle cramps, headache, and dizziness. The person is still alert and able to talk to you.What to do: move the person to shade or air conditioning, loosen tight clothing, give cool water or an electrolyte drink in small sips, and apply cool wet cloths to the neck, armpits, and wrists. Reassess in 15 to 30 minutes. If symptoms do not improve, get medical care.Heat stroke: call 911 immediatelySigns include a body temperature of 103°F or higher, hot red skin that may be either dry or moist, a fast strong pulse, confusion or slurred speech, agitation, seizures, or loss of consciousness.What to do: call 911 first. Move the person to shade and remove outer clothing. Soak the skin with cool water or apply ice packs to the neck, armpits, and groin. Do not give fluids if the person cannot swallow safely. Stay with them until help arrives.The CDC’s emergency warning page on extreme heat has more detail on each scenario and is worth saving on your phone before any World Cup match day.What Should I Bring to a World Cup Match in Arlington?The CDC recommends drinking about 8 ounces of water every 15 to 20 minutes during outdoor activity in extreme heat. For a typical match day with pre-game tailgating and walk-in, plan on 80 to 120 ounces total fluid. Pack a hat, sunscreen, an electrolyte drink, and a battery fan. Check the FIFA and AT&T Stadium bag and bottle policies before you go (rules tighten for major events).A practical World Cup match day kit:Reusable or sealed water bottle (confirm allowed type with stadium and FIFA before kickoff)Electrolyte tablets or powder (sodium, potassium, magnesium)Wide-brim hat or capSunscreen SPF 30 or higher, reapplied every two hoursBattery-powered hand fanLight-colored, loose, breathable clothing (your team kit if it is breathable; avoid heavy synthetic jerseys in direct sun)Cooling towel (soak in cold water, drape on neck)Snacks with sodium (pretzels, trail mix)SunglassesHow Much Water Do I Actually Need During a World Cup Match Day?For a full match day (2-3 hours of pre-match plus a 2-hour match plus walk-out), plan on 80 to 120 ounces of fluid total. The American College of Sports Medicine recommends starting hydrated, drinking 16 to 24 ounces two hours before the activity, then 4 to 8 ounces every 15 minutes during. Plain water alone is not enough for sustained heat exposure over two hours. You also need electrolytes.What Should I Do If I Feel Sick at the Stadium or FanFest?Get to shade or an air-conditioned area immediately (the concourses at AT&T Stadium are air-conditioned). Drink cool water with electrolytes if you can swallow safely. Apply a wet cloth to your neck and wrists. Tell someone with you what you are feeling and ask them to stay close. If symptoms do not improve in 15 to 30 minutes, ask stadium first-aid staff for help or leave for medical care.What Helps Recovery After a Long Match Day in Texas Heat?Mild dehydration usually resolves with rest, fluids, and electrolytes over a few hours. Drink water with added sodium and potassium. Eat foods with high water content such as watermelon, cucumber, or broth. The MedlinePlus reference on electrolytes explains why sodium and potassium replacement matter as much as fluid volume.For visitors and locals with persistent symptoms after a long match day (headache, dizziness, dark urine that does not normalize after eight hours), oral rehydration is sometimes not enough. Options include faster oral rehydration solutions, urgent care evaluation, or IV fluid therapy at a hydration clinic. Our IV therapy program in Irving sits 15 minutes from AT&T Stadium and offers blends that combine saline with B vitamins, amino acids, and electrolytes for faster rehydration than drinking water alone. Visitors traveling to multiple matches across host cities sometimes book a recovery session between match days to reset before the next outing.When Should I Go to the ER vs Urgent Care vs a Hydration Clinic?Call 911 or go to the nearest ER for confusion, stopped sweating, body temperature above 103°F, chest pain, or fainting. Urgent care fits heat exhaustion symptoms that have not improved with rest and fluids in 30 minutes. A hydration clinic is appropriate for mild post-match recovery in an otherwise healthy adult without red-flag symptoms.ER or call 911:Confusion, agitation, or loss of consciousnessHot dry skin with body temperature above 103°FChest pain or pressureSeizureVomiting that prevents fluid intakeAny of the above in a child under 4, an adult over 65, or a person with heart, kidney, or diabetes historyUrgent care:Heat exhaustion symptoms not improving in 30 minutes with rest and oral fluidsPersistent nausea or vomitingSevere muscle cramps that do not relax with rest and hydrationMild confusion that clears with rest in air conditioningHydration clinic (IV therapy):Mild post-match fatigue and a “wrung out” feelingMild dehydration in an otherwise healthy adultYou can drink, walk, and think clearly, but feel slow to recoverFrequently Asked QuestionsI am visiting Arlington from a cooler country for a World Cup match. How do I prepare for the heat?Heat acclimatization takes 7 to 14 days of gradual exposure per CDC guidance. Most visitors will not have that runway. Practical steps: start increasing your daily water intake the moment you land, spend short periods outdoors in early-morning or evening hours to begin adapting, avoid alcohol on travel and match days, eat foods with salt, and plan air-conditioned breaks every couple of hours on match day. Pace yourself.The match roof at AT&T Stadium will probably be closed. Why do I still need to worry about heat?The match itself may be in air conditioning, but pre-match tailgating, walking from parking to the gates, post-match walk-out, outdoor FanFest events, and any sightseeing before or after the match all happen in full Texas summer heat. Most heat illness happens outside the match, not in the stands.Is it safe to drink coffee or energy drinks at a World Cup match in the heat?Both contain caffeine, a mild diuretic. The American Heart Association notes that caffeine does not significantly worsen dehydration for healthy adults at moderate doses (under 400 mg per day). However, large energy drinks combined with heat and alcohol can stress the cardiovascular system. One cup of coffee or one energy drink during the day is reasonable. Multiples are not.Can I just drink water, or do I need electrolytes?For sustained heat exposure over two hours, electrolytes matter. Sweat removes sodium, potassium, and magnesium along with water. Replacing only water can rarely cause hyponatremia (low blood sodium), which has its own dangerous symptoms (nausea, confusion, in severe cases seizures). A simple electrolyte tablet in your water bottle is enough for most spectators.How long does it take to recover from heat exhaustion?With rest in a cool environment, fluids, and electrolyte replacement, mild heat exhaustion usually resolves in a few hours. Some people feel washed out for one to two days afterward. If symptoms persist past 24 hours or worsen, see a clinician. Travelers attending consecutive match days should not “push through” a bad recovery day; build in true rest.Are kids and older adults at higher risk at outdoor matches?Yes. The CDC identifies children under 4, adults over 65, people with cardiovascular disease, and those on certain medications (diuretics, some blood pressure medications, some psychiatric medications) as higher-risk. Watch them closely, ensure they drink frequently, and move them to shade or air conditioning sooner than you think you need to.I am going to a FIFA FanFest instead of a stadium match. Is that safer in the heat?Not necessarily. FanFests are typically outdoors. The watching crowd often stands for two hours, sometimes without shade. Same rules apply: 8 ounces of water every 15 to 20 minutes, a hat, electrolytes, sunscreen, and a battery fan. Plan for the same total fluid intake as you would for a stadium match.Should I get an IV before the match as a “pre-load”?For healthy spectators, the answer is generally no. Drinking water with electrolytes the day before and the morning of the match is sufficient. IV hydration is more appropriate for recovery if someone becomes significantly dehydrated, or for visitors who arrive already depleted from long travel. It is not routine pre-event prep.If you or someone with you shows signs of heat stroke (confusion, hot dry skin, body temperature above 103°F), call 911 immediately. This article is for general informational purposes and does not replace medical evaluation. What Makes Microneedling FDA-Cleared?Microneedling devices used in our clinic are FDA-cleared as Class II medical devices for treating acne scars, fine lines, stretch marks, and pigmentation concerns under regulatory oversight on needle depth, sterility, and infection control. Three numbers worth knowing. FDA Class II Medical-device classification when needle depth exceeds 0.3mm. Subject to FDA premarket clearance and post-market device-tracking requirements. 0.5 to 2.5 mm Approved needle depths used for facial and body indications. We adjust depth based on the area being treated, skin thickness, and your tolerance. 3 to 6 sessions Standard series for full collagen remodeling. Sessions are spaced 4 to 6 weeks apart so new collagen has time to form before the next pass.What Are the Most Common Microneedling Myths?Here are the four misconceptions we hear most often, with the clinical context behind each. Myth: It's the same as a derma roller Fact: Professional microneedling uses sterile single-use cartridges with needles up to 2.5 mm under controlled depth. At-home derma rollers rarely reach the dermis and can cross-contaminate. Myth: More bleeding equals better results Fact: Pinpoint bleeding signals correct dermal depth, not efficacy. Collagen induction depends on controlled microinjury, not blood volume. Myth: Sensitive skin cannot be treated Fact: Sensitive skin can be treated with shorter needle depths and longer healing intervals. We screen for active eczema, rosacea flares, and isotretinoin use within the past 6 months. Myth: Results show up overnight Fact: New collagen takes 4 to 6 weeks to remodel. Peak results from a single session appear at month 3 to 6. A series of 3 to 6 sessions produces the strongest long-term outcome. Here is a step-by-step guide to your visit so you know exactly what to anticipate. Skin Consultation Your nurse reviews your skin history, current routine, sun exposure, and any active conditions. We confirm microneedling is the right fit for your skin and explain the plan before we begin. The Treatment Cleanse, topical numbing applied, then the microneedling device passes across the treatment area in controlled rows. Most patients describe a warm, prickly sensation that fades quickly. Aftercare Mild redness or warmth may follow for 24 to 48 hours. Apply broad-spectrum SPF, skip retinoids and exfoliating acids for 48 hours, and resume your normal routine the same day or next morning.How Does the Microneedling Healing Process Work?Here is the typical recovery and remodeling timeline for a standard 1.0 to 1.5 mm microneedling session. Hours 0 to 24 Pinpoint bleeding stops within hours. Skin appears flushed with mild swelling, similar to a moderate sunburn. Days 1 to 3 Redness fades to a mild pink. Skin feels tight, slightly rough, and warm. Use gentle moisturizer and SPF only. Days 4 to 7 Light sloughing of dead skin reveals smoother texture. Resume normal skincare; avoid retinoids and chemical acids. Weeks 2 to 4 Initial brightness and refined pores become visible. Collagen remodeling begins. Avoid direct sun exposure to protect new skin. Months 3 to 6 Peak collagen and elastin remodeling produces lifted, smooth skin. Schedule maintenance every 4 to 6 months or after a 3-session series.Conveniently Located for DFW ProfessionalsYour time is valuable. What is microneedling and how does it work? Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, uses a medical-grade device with very fine sterile needles to create thousands of controlled micro-channels in the upper layer of the skin. Your body responds by producing new collagen and elastin during the healing process, which gradually smooths texture, softens scars, and improves overall tone. The actual treatment time is roughly 30 to 45 minutes after numbing. How many microneedling sessions will I need? Most patients see meaningful improvement after a series of 3 sessions spaced 4 to 6 weeks apart, which is why we offer both single treatments and 3-session packages. Patients treating deeper acne scarring or significant texture concerns may benefit from 4 to 6 sessions, and we will outline a realistic plan during your consultation based on your skin and goals. What is the downtime after microneedling? Downtime is minimal for most patients. Expect mild redness and a sunburn-like warmth for 24 to 48 hours, with possible light flaking around day 3. Most people return to work or normal activities the next day. Avoid retinoids, exfoliating acids, and direct sun exposure for at least 48 hours, and apply broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher whenever you go outside. Should I book an appointment for microneedling? Yes. Microneedling is a planned procedure, so booking in advance protects your spot. It also gives us time to review your skin history before the session. If you have a special event coming up, call us at least 2 to 3 weeks ahead. That way we can sequence your treatments for the best result on the day that matters. Is microneedling safe for sensitive skin? For most patients with sensitive skin, yes. Microneedling is well tolerated when performed by a trained clinician at appropriate needle depths. During your consultation we review any history of rosacea, active acne flares, eczema, recent isotretinoin use, or current cold sores. Those situations change either the timing or the depth we choose. If microneedling is not the right fit on the day of your visit, we will tell you upfront and discuss alternatives.

Each area uses a different unit range based on muscle strength and your aesthetic goals.Forehead Lines10-20 UNITSSoftens the horizontal lines that form across the forehead when you raise your eyebrows.Glabellar "11" Lines15-25 UNITSTargets the vertical frown lines between the brows that deepen with concentration or stress.Crow's Feet10-15 PER SIDESmooths the fine lines fanning out from the outer corners of the eyes when you smile.Lip Flip4-8 UNITSSubtly relaxes the upper lip border so it appears slightly fuller without adding filler volume.Brow Lift4-8 UNITSA subtle Botox brow lift opens the eye area and creates a refreshed, less-tired appearance.How Botox Works Botox is the brand name for onabotulinumtoxinA, a purified neuromodulator FDA-approved for cosmetic use since 2002. Micro-injections temporarily block signals between nerve and muscle, allowing the overlying skin to smooth out.Phase 01The MechanismTargets one muscle at a time Botulinum toxin type A blocks acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction. The muscle relaxes; the wrinkle softens. Surrounding expression stays intact. NCBI clinical reference.Phase 02Onset and DurationVisible by day 10, lasts 3-4 months Initial smoothing begins around day 3 to 4. Full effect appears by day 10 to 14. Most patients see 3 to 4 months of result before the muscle gradually regains function.Phase 03Safety Profile23+ years of clinical use With more than two decades of cosmetic use, Botox has one of the most extensively studied safety profiles in aesthetic medicine. Side effects are rare and typically mild when administered by a trained medical practitioner, consistent with American Academy of Dermatology safety guidance.Visible Effect TimelineWhat to Expect Day by Day After Your Botox TreatmentMost pages tell you Botox takes "3 to 7 days" to show. The real timeline is more nuanced. Here is exactly what happens at each stage so you know what is normal and when to call us.Day 0Day 3-7Day 10-14Month 1-3Month 3-4Day 0Treatment DayInjection takes 10 to 15 minutes. Small raised bumps at injection points are normal and fade within 30 to 60 minutes. No visible smoothing yet. Avoid lying down or vigorous exercise for 4 hours.Day 3 to 4First Muscle RelaxationTreated muscles begin to relax. You may notice a subtle softening when you frown or raise your eyebrows. Resting lines look about the same. This is the earliest a non-clinician might detect a change.Day 5 to 7Visible Smoothing BeginsFriends and family often start commenting around this window. Dynamic wrinkles soften noticeably. Patients typically describe feeling lighter in the treated areas, like the muscles are resting.Day 10 to 14Full Effect & Touch-Up WindowPeak neuromodulator effect. Forehead and glabellar lines appear smoothest now. This is when your complimentary 2-week follow-up happens at our Irving clinic. Any minor asymmetry is corrected at no additional charge.Month 1 to 2Optimal Result HoldingSkin texture in treated areas reaches its smoothest appearance and holds. This is the window where patients photograph results and feel most confident about the investment.Month 3First Signs of ReturnSubtle muscle activity begins to reappear, especially in highly expressive patients. Some dynamic movement returns before any visible lines. Time to schedule your next consultation.Month 3 to 4Time to Re-TreatMost patients schedule re-treatment in this window. Treating before complete return often means future treatments need fewer units, because treated muscles gradually weaken with consistent disuse.Beyond 4 MonthsWhat If You Skip?Muscles return to baseline function. Wrinkles return gradually, not worse than before. Years of consistent treatment may reduce baseline static lines because treated muscles slightly atrophy with disuse.Clinical & Regulatory Track RecordBotox Cosmetic: Two Decades of FDA-Cleared UseBotulinum toxin type A is one of the most studied molecules in aesthetic medicine. Below is a synthesized timeline of FDA milestones and US treatment volume, with sources you can verify.YearMilestoneClinical DetailSource1989FDA approval of botulinum toxin type A for medical use (strabismus and blepharospasm)First therapeutic use established years before cosmetic applicationFDA Drugs@FDA2002FDA approval for cosmetic use on glabellar lines (the "11" lines between brows)Foundational cosmetic indication; based on Phase III randomized controlled trialsFDA Drugs@FDA2013Approval extended to lateral canthal lines (crow's feet)Second cosmetic indication after a decade of off-label useFDA Drugs@FDA2017Approval extended to forehead lines (horizontal lines)Third cosmetic indication. Most commonly treated area todayFDA Drugs@FDA20249.5+ million neurotoxin treatments performed in the US in a single yearBotulinum toxin type A remains the #1 minimally invasive cosmetic procedure for the 23rd consecutive yearASPS Statistics2025Average first-time cosmetic neurotoxin patient is 35 years oldPreventative ("baby") Botox starting in late 20s drives demographic shiftAAFPRS CensusSynthesized from public FDA, American Society of Plastic Surgeons, and American Academy of Facial Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery data.Common MisconceptionsBotox Myths vs Clinical FactsSix misconceptions we field at every Irving consultation, answered with the clinical references behind each correction.Myth"Botox is dangerous because it's a toxin."FactBotulinum toxin type A used cosmetically is purified, FDA-cleared since 2002, and administered in micro-doses (typically 10 to 30 units per area). Each unit contains nanogram-level quantities of active protein, far below any threshold for systemic concern when administered by a trained clinician.Source: NCBI StatPearls clinical referenceMyth"Botox will make my face look frozen or expressionless."FactFrozen results come from over-dosing or imprecise injection placement, not from Botox itself. Anatomy-mapped dosing by a Board Certified clinician produces selective muscle relaxation while preserving natural expression. Our 2-week follow-up exists specifically to catch any asymmetry early.Source: American Academy of Dermatology guidanceMyth"If I stop Botox, my wrinkles will come back worse than before."FactStopping Botox returns muscles to baseline function. Wrinkles return gradually over 3 to 4 months, not worse than they were originally. Long-term consistent use can actually reduce baseline static lines because treated muscles atrophy slightly with disuse.Source: NCBI clinical review on neuromodulator pharmacologyMyth"Botox is only for older women."FactThe average first-time cosmetic neurotoxin patient is 35 years old. Preventative or "baby" Botox in the late 20s is increasingly common and trains muscles before deep static lines form. Men account for roughly 7% of treatments and that share is growing yearly.Source: AAFPRS Annual CensusMyth"More units mean better results."FactOptimal results come from matching dose to specific muscle strength, not from maximizing units. Most forehead patients need 10 to 20 units, glabellar 15 to 25, crow's feet 10 to 15 per side. Over-dosing produces frozen expressions, not better smoothing.Source: FDA Botox prescribing informationMyth"Telehealth Botox is the same as in-clinic."FactBotox requires an in-person injection by a trained clinician. No legitimate telehealth provider ships Botox for self-injection because the procedure requires anatomy mapping, sterile administration, and immediate clinician oversight for adverse events. Any service claiming otherwise is operating outside FDA-cleared protocols.Source: AAD patient safety guidanceWhat to Expect at Your Appointment From consultation to follow-up, here is exactly how your Botox visit unfolds.115-20 MINConsultationLori reviews your aesthetic goals, medical history, and any prior injectable experience. Any minor asymmetry is corrected with a touch-up at no additional charge.Meet Your ProviderExpert Care Led by Lori Secerovic, APRN Anatomy-led dosing produces softer wrinkles, not frozen expressions. Every Botox treatment is grounded in clinical science and tailored to your face.Lead ClinicianLori Secerovic, FNP-C, MSN With a background rooted in high-acuity critical care at the University of Chicago, Lori brings the precision of clinical medicine to aesthetic injectables. text: How to Choose a Weight Loss Clinic: 7 Questions to Ask First By Irving H&W Clinic May 8, 2026 Medical Weight Loss Table of Contents Key Takeaways:Most weight loss clinics oversell results and undersell the medical workup that drives them.A real medical program starts with bloodwork, not a sales pitch.Compounded GLP-1 is not the same product as FDA-approved Ozempic, Mounjaro, or Wegovy.Transparent pricing, board-certified providers, and a written maintenance plan are the three biggest signals of a serious clinic.The right program addresses why your body is holding weight, not just calorie math. Searching for a weight loss clinic feels like buying a car with a blindfold on. Every site claims rapid results, every clinic offers some version of GLP-1 medication, and every program looks identical from the outside. The differences are real, and they matter. This guide gives you 7 specific questions to ask before you write the first check.Ask thisA serious clinic’s answerAre providers board-certified?Credentials listed publicly, verifiable on the state boardDoes it start with bloodwork?Thyroid, fasting insulin, HbA1c, hormones before any prescriptionFDA-approved or compounded GLP-1?Brand-name products, answer given in writingIs pricing transparent?Flat monthly cost stated in the first conversationIs there a written maintenance plan?Taper protocol and check-ins defined before you startHow are results measured?Body composition and labs, not scale weight aloneHow is this different from a diet?A specific answer about testing and treating causesWhy Picking the Right Clinic MattersA poor choice costs more than money. The wrong clinic delays real progress, prescribes medications without testing, skips the maintenance phase, and the rebound weight gain hits harder than the original loss.The opposite is also true. A solid medical weight loss program can produce sustainable results that diet apps and gyms cannot.Question 1: Are the Providers Board-Certified?Weight loss is medicine. Hormones, insulin, and metabolic markers all get adjusted along the way. The clinician running your plan should be a board-certified MD, DO, or NP, not a coach with a certificate from a weekend course.Verify board certification on the state medical board website. Any real clinic will list provider credentials publicly.“The best weight loss programs are the academic programs or community programs attached to a medical center run by obesity medicine specialists that offer lifestyle medications, psychology and metabolic surgery options.”Dr. Caroline Apovian, professor of medicine, Harvard Medical School | TODAYThe principle scales down: medical oversight first, marketing second.Question 2: Does the Program Start with Bloodwork?Any clinic that prescribes GLP-1 or Lipo-B without first running a thyroid panel, fasting insulin, HbA1c, and a hormone panel is treating symptoms, not causes. Your body may be holding weight because of insulin resistance, low thyroid, perimenopause, or chronic cortisol. The medication that actually helps depends on which one applies.Our explainer on hormones and weight gain walks through the most common metabolic drivers and the labs that catch them.Question 3: Is the GLP-1 FDA-Approved or Compounded?Compounded GLP-1 medications are not the same product as Ozempic, Mounjaro, or Wegovy. Compounded versions often use different active forms, different concentrations, and different fillers. Some patients tolerate them well. Others do not.If a clinic offers GLP-1 at a price point that feels too good to be true, it is almost certainly compounded. Ask directly. The answer should be in writing.The FDA publishes safety alerts on compounded semaglutide. Read those before signing up.“Any legitimate medical weight loss program today should offer FDA-approved, brand-name GLP-1 therapies.”Dr. Christopher McGowan, gastroenterologist and obesity medicine specialist | TODAYQuestion 4: Is Pricing Transparent or Hidden?Run a mental stopwatch on this one. A real clinic gives you a flat monthly cost in the first conversation. A red-flag clinic hides pricing behind a free consultation that turns into a sales pitch. We hold ourselves to this test: our consultations are free for every patient, and program pricing is stated before you commit to anything.Specifically ask:What is the monthly program cost?What does that include (visits, medication, follow-up)?What costs extra (bloodwork, body composition scans, supplements)?Is there a contract or month-to-month billing?What is the cancellation policy?Question 5: Is There a Written Maintenance Plan?Most programs market the loss phase. Few talk about what happens after. Ask the clinic exactly what their maintenance protocol looks like:How are doses tapered?What happens when the medication stops?What lifestyle anchors does the program build before you exit?How often do you check in during maintenance?If a clinic shrugs at the maintenance question, the program is built to lose you weight and then lose you as a patient. Our breakdown of long-term maintenance habits covers what real maintenance looks like.Question 6: How Are Results Measured?Scale weight is a noisy signal. Real medical programs track:Body composition (lean mass vs fat mass)Waist circumferenceResting metabolic rateBloodwork progress (insulin, HbA1c, lipids)If the only number a clinic celebrates is the scale, expect rebound. Muscle loss disguised as weight loss is the most common failure mode of mass-market programs.Question 7: How Is the Program Different from a Diet?This is the litmus question. A real clinic should be able to answer in 30 seconds, with specifics. Diets target calories. Medical weight loss targets the metabolic blocks that make calorie restriction fail.If the answer is “we just give you GLP-1,” it is not a medical program. If the answer is “we test, we treat the cause, and we adjust,” that is the real thing. Our piece on medical weight loss vs dieting covers the full distinction.Red Flags to Walk Away FromSkip any clinic that does any of these:Promises a specific number (“Lose 30 lbs in 30 days”).Charges for the consultation without telling you the program cost first.Refuses to run bloodwork before prescribing.Pushes a long-term contract.Uses generic stock photos with zero provider credentials on the site.The CDC recommends 1 to 2 pounds per week as the safe, sustainable rate. Anyone promising more is selling fluid loss as fat loss.Frequently Asked QuestionsIs it worth paying for a medical weight loss program?For patients with metabolic drivers (insulin resistance, thyroid issues, hormonal shifts, PCOS, perimenopause), yes. Diet alone usually fails when the body has a medical reason to hold weight. For patients without those drivers, a structured fitness coach or app may be enough.How much should a real weight loss program cost?Bloodwork-only programs run $150 to $300 per month. Programs with prescriptions usually fall between $200 and $600 per month, plus the cost of the medication. Anything substantially cheaper usually skips the medical component.Should I trust online-only weight loss programs?Online programs work for follow-up visits, but the initial workup benefits from in-person bloodwork and body composition. Hybrid programs (in-person intake, virtual follow-ups) usually outperform fully remote programs for stubborn weight.What questions should I ask in the first consultation?Use the 7 questions above. Add: Will I see the same provider every visit? Who do I contact if a medication causes side effects? What happens if I plateau?How do I choose the right clinic for GLP-1 weight loss treatment?Apply the same seven questions, with two extra filters: the clinic should run labs before prescribing, and it should offer FDA-approved products rather than compounded copies. Then ask which medication fits your case and why. Our semaglutide vs tirzepatide comparison shows the trial data a good clinic will walk you through.How long should I stay on GLP-1 medication?Most patients stay on a maintenance dose long-term. Stopping the medication entirely often leads to weight regain. A real clinic builds your taper and maintenance plan from day one.Ready to Talk to a Real Medical Weight Loss Team?If you want a program that starts with labs, treats the cause, and includes a written maintenance plan, our medical weight loss team in Irving handles all of it under one roof. Book a consultation and bring these 7 questions with you. Expert Verified Content — Reviewed: May 8, 2026 Medically Reviewed & Partnered In Your Progress.This guidance was reviewed by Lori Secerovic, APRN, FNP-C, MSN, to ensure clinical safety. Practicing since 2009, with 17+ years of critical-care experience now applied to evidence-based hormone optimization, thyroid management, and integrative wellness. 17+Years Clinical ExperienceICUCritical Care BackgroundFNP-CBoard CertifiedTXLicensed APRN Clinical Profile / OverviewLori Secerovic, APRN, FNP-C, MSN joined Irving Health and Wellness Clinic in December 2025 as our lead Family Nurse Practitioner. Patients see her for the clinic’s full range of wellness services.Patients across Irving, Las Colinas, Coppell, Valley Ranch, and the wider Dallas metroplex see her for comprehensive wellness, hormone, and aesthetic care under one roof. Integrated with medical care rather than offered as a standalone program. What conditions does Lori treat? / Scope of practiceLori is licensed as a Family Nurse Practitioner with APRN designation and DEA prescriptive authority in Texas. She treats adult and pediatric primary-care conditions plus the clinic’s wellness specialties: hormone imbalance, hypothyroidism, obesity and metabolic syndrome, and age-related concerns.
